questions.question: Which property causes objects to gravitationally attract each other in Newton's model?
What is a gravitational field?
choices: A region where all objects have the same mass
A force produced only by magnets
A description of gravitational force per unit mass at each location
An area with no possible acceleration

questions.question: Which direction does centripetal acceleration point?
choices: Toward the center of the circular path

questions.question: What does orbital period measure?
What does free fall mean in an ideal introductory model?
What is a tangent to a circular path at a point?
choices: A line in the instantaneous direction of motion
A line pointing only toward the center
The diameter through all possible points
The distance around the whole circle

questions.question: Which relation gives centripetal acceleration for speed v and radius r?
Why does uniform circular motion involve acceleration?
choices: Acceleration requires an increase in speed only
The object stays at one position

questions.question: Why is centripetal force not a separate new kind of interaction?
choices: It acts only when no other forces exist
It names the inward net-force role that gravity, tension, or other forces can provide
It is always opposite the net force
It is generated solely by circular motion

questions.question: Why can a satellite remain in orbit while continuously falling?
choices: Gravity is absent at orbital height
Its mass becomes zero in orbit
Its forward motion carries it around Earth as gravity accelerates it inward

questions.question: How does gravitational force change if one mass doubles and separation stays fixed?
How does gravitational attraction change if center-to-center distance doubles, with masses fixed?
choices: It becomes four times as large

questions.question: Why do astronauts in a freely falling orbital station feel weightless?
choices: They and their surroundings accelerate together without ordinary support forces

questions.question: Why do objects of different masses fall with the same acceleration in a vacuum near Earth?
choices: Gravitational force and inertia both scale with mass
The heavier object has no gravitational force
The lighter object has a larger downward net force

questions.question: What happens to a circular-motion requirement if speed increases but radius stays fixed?
choices: A larger inward acceleration is needed

questions.question: A satellite has constant speed in a circular orbit. Which quantity changes?
Using a = v²/r, what is the inward acceleration at 4 m/s on a 2 m radius path?
A ball's supporting string breaks during horizontal circular motion. Neglect other forces for the instant afterward. Which direction does it initially move?
Two identical masses move from separation r to separation 3r. What fraction of the original gravitational force remains?
A car rounds a level curve at constant speed. What provides the needed horizontal inward force in the usual no-skidding model?
choices: The road's upward normal force alone
